title: Ke kālā a me ke kūʻai ʻana
description: Ten short stories about money and shopping: birthday money in a toy shop, a girl's first fishhooks and fish sold by the pound, a pig bought for a family imu, saving in a bank account for a telescope, a boastful noni seller at the market, plants from a nursery, a hand-sewn malo instead of a dear one, a craft fair in an old fort, gifts for a baptism and a grandmother's dish bought and cooked after her funeral.

lessons.title: Nā holoholona o ka hale kūʻai mea pāʻani
lessons.summary: For his eighth birthday Kekaimalu gets twenty dollars from his grandmother Kaleimomi; in a Honolulu toy shop he looks at a polar bear, a dolphin, a fox, a Hawaiian crow and a triggerfish, buys a dugong for nineteen dollars, and his grandmother buys a small dolphin for his sister Pualei.
lessons.text:
Ua piha ʻewalu makahiki o Kekaimalu. Ma kona lā hānau, ua hāʻawi kona kupuna wahine ʻo Kaleimomi iā ia i 20 kālā. "Noʻu kēia kālā?" i nīnau ai ʻo Kekaimalu. "ʻAe," wahi a Kaleimomi. "Hiki iā ʻoe ke kūʻai i kekahi mea pāʻani āu e makemake ai." I ka Pōʻaono, ua hele lāua i kekahi hale kūʻai mea pāʻani ma Honolulu.

Ma nā papa o ka hale kūʻai, aia nā holoholona pāʻani he nui. Aia kekahi nanuka keʻokeʻo nui, kekahi hoikiuna uliuli, kekahi ʻalopeka ʻulaʻula, a me kekahi ʻalalā ʻeleʻele. Aia pū kekahi humuhumunukunukuāpuaʻa liʻiliʻi me nā kala he nui. "ʻO ka humuhumunukunukuāpuaʻa ka iʻa o ko kākou mokuʻāina," wahi a Kaleimomi. "A ʻo ka ʻalalā, he manu no Hawaiʻi wale nō."

Ua lawe ʻo Kekaimalu i kekahi holoholona hina me ka ihu nui. Ua hele mai kekahi wahine o ka hale kūʻai. "He kūionoko kēnā," wahi āna. "Noho ke kūionoko ma nā kai mehana ma kahi mamao, a ʻai ʻo ia i ka mauʻu o lalo o ke kai. He ʻumikūmāiwa kālā ke kumukūʻai o kēnā kūionoko."

Ua nānā ʻo Kekaimalu i nā holoholona a pau. He 25 kālā ka nanuka, ʻoi aku ma mua o kāna kālā. He 12 kālā ka ʻalopeka, a he 10 kālā ka ʻalalā. Ua paʻa naʻe ʻo ia i ke kūionoko. "Noʻu ke kūionoko!" wahi āna. Ua uku ʻo ia i ka ʻumikūmāiwa kālā, a ua koe hoʻokahi kālā ma kona lima.

Ma ka puka, ua ʻike ʻo Kekaimalu i kekahi hoikiuna liʻiliʻi ma kekahi papa. "Makemake nui koʻu kaikuahine ʻo Pualei i nā hoikiuna," wahi āna, "akā hoʻokahi wale nō kālā i koe iaʻu." Ua ʻakaʻaka ʻo Kaleimomi. "ʻŌlelo kekahi poʻe he pī ʻo Tūtū, akā ʻaʻole au pī i kaʻu mau moʻopuna," wahi āna. ʻAʻole ʻo Kekaimalu he keiki pī: ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i kāna kālā hope loa iā Tūtū, a ua kūʻai ʻo Kaleimomi i ka hoikiuna liʻiliʻi no Pualei.

Ma ka hale, ua hāʻawi ʻo Kekaimalu i ka hoikiuna iā Pualei. "Noʻu kēia?" i nīnau ai ʻo ia. "Nou ka hoikiuna, a noʻu ke kūionoko," wahi a Kekaimalu.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia kālā i hāʻawi ai ʻo Kaleimomi iā Kekaimalu?
Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia iā ia i 20 kālā.
He aha ka iʻa o ka mokuʻāina?
ʻO ka humuhumunukunukuāpuaʻa ka iʻa o ka mokuʻāina.
Noho ke kūionoko ma hea?
Noho ke kūionoko ma nā kai mehana ma kahi mamao.
No ke aha ʻaʻole ʻo Kekaimalu i kūʻai i ka nanuka?
No ka mea, ua ʻoi aku ke kumukūʻai o ka nanuka ma mua o kāna kālā.
Na wai i kūʻai i ka hoikiuna liʻiliʻi?
Na Kaleimomi i kūʻai i ka hoikiuna liʻiliʻi no Pualei.

lessons.title: Nā makau mua o Kuʻuwehi
lessons.summary: Kahinu, a muscular truck driver in Waiʻanae, drives his daughter Kuʻuwehi to buy her first fishhooks and line; she catches three mullet, sells two by the pound at the fish market, and at home her father crushes the coarse salt for the big one.
lessons.text:
He kanaka konakona ʻo Kahinu. Kalaiwa ʻo ia i kekahi kalaka nui no kekahi hui ma Waiʻanae, a hāpai ʻo ia i nā pahu kaumaha i kēlā me kēia lā. I kekahi Pōʻaono, ua kalaiwa ʻo ia i kona kalaka me kāna kaikamahine ʻo Kuʻuwehi i kekahi hale kūʻai lako lawaiʻa. ʻAkahi nō ʻo Kuʻuwehi a hele i ka lawaiʻa, a ua hauʻoli loa ʻo ia.

Ma ka hale kūʻai, ua koho lāua i ʻelima makau liʻiliʻi a me kekahi aho lōʻihi. "He ʻelua kālā no nā makau ʻelima, a he ʻewalu kālā no ke aho," wahi a ka mea kūʻai. Ua uku ʻo Kuʻuwehi me kāna kālā ponoʻī. "ʻAkahi nō au a kūʻai i kaʻu mau makau ponoʻī!" wahi āna.

Ua kalaiwa lāua i kahakai, kokoke i ka nuku o kekahi kahawai. Ua hoʻopaʻa ʻo Kahinu i kekahi makau ma ke aho. Ua kiola ʻo Kuʻuwehi i ke aho i loko o ka wai. Ma hope o ka hapalua hola, ua huki ikaika ʻia ke aho. "He iʻa!" wahi a Kuʻuwehi. Ua huki ʻo ia i ke aho, a aia ma ka makau kekahi ʻanae nui. Ma mua o ke awakea, ua loaʻa iā ia ʻekolu ʻanae.

Ma ka hoʻi ʻana, ua kū lāua ma kekahi mākeke iʻa. Ua kau ka mea kūʻai iʻa i nā ʻanae ma luna o ke kaupaona. "ʻEkolu paona kēia ʻanae nui, a ʻelua paona ko kēlā me kēia ʻanae liʻiliʻi," wahi āna. "E uku au i ʻelima kālā no ka paona." Ua kūʻai aku ʻo Kuʻuwehi i nā ʻanae liʻiliʻi ʻelua, a ua loaʻa iā ia he 20 kālā. Ua kūʻai pū lāua i ʻelua paona paʻakai.

Ua nui loa nā ʻāpana o ka paʻakai, no laila ua hōʻae ʻo Kahinu i ka paʻakai me kekahi pōhaku liʻiliʻi, a liʻiliʻi loa ka paʻakai. Ua hōʻae ʻo ia me kona mau lima konakona, a ua ʻakaʻaka ʻo Kuʻuwehi. A laila, ua kau ʻo Kuʻuwehi i ka paʻakai ma luna o ka ʻanae nui, a ua kuke lāua iā ia ma luna o ke ahi. "ʻAkahi nō au a ʻai i ka iʻa i loaʻa iaʻu," wahi a Kuʻuwehi.

Nā nīnau:
He aha nā mea a Kuʻuwehi i kūʻai ai ma ka hale kūʻai lako lawaiʻa?
Ua kūʻai ʻo ia i ʻelima makau liʻiliʻi a me kekahi aho lōʻihi.
ʻEhia ʻanae i loaʻa iā Kuʻuwehi?
Ua loaʻa iā ia ʻekolu ʻanae.
ʻEhia kālā no ka paona i uku ai ka mea kūʻai iʻa?
Ua uku ʻo ia i ʻelima kālā no ka paona.
No ke aha i hōʻae ai ʻo Kahinu i ka paʻakai?
No ka mea, ua nui loa nā ʻāpana o ka paʻakai.

lessons.title: Ka imu o nā pilikana
lessons.summary: Kealiʻinui buys a pig and breadfruit for the yearly gathering of his relatives in Kaʻū; with his son Kaʻimikaua he digs the imu, lights the fire, lays the pig on the hot stones and lets the steam cook it, lets the meat cool before cutting, and the next day warms up the cold leftovers.
lessons.text:
I kēlā me kēia makahiki, hui pū nā pilikana a pau o Kealiʻinui ma Kaʻū no ka lā hānau o ko lākou kupuna. I kēia makahiki, ua kūʻai ʻo Kealiʻinui i kekahi puaʻa mai kekahi mahiʻai no 300 kālā. Ua uku kēlā me kēia ʻohana i kekahi hapa o ke kumukūʻai. Ua kūʻai pū ʻo ia i ʻumi ʻulu ma ka mākeke.

Ma ke kakahiaka nui, ua ʻeli ʻo Kealiʻinui me kāna keiki ʻo Kaʻimikaua i kekahi lua ma ka lepo: ʻo ia ka imu. Ua hoʻonoho lāua i ka wahie a me nā pōhaku i loko o ka imu. A laila, ua hōʻā ʻo Kealiʻinui i ka wahie. Ua piʻi ka uahi i ka lani. Ua ʻike ʻia ka uahi e nā kānaka o ke kaiāulu.

No ʻelua hola, ua hoʻopumehana ke ahi i nā pōhaku a wela loa lākou. Ua kau lāua i nā lau maiʻa ma luna o nā pōhaku wela, a laila ka puaʻa a me nā ʻulu. Ua uhi lāua i ka imu me nā lau a me ka lepo. Ua piʻi aʻe ka māhu mai loko mai o ka lepo. "ʻO ka māhu ka mea e kālua ai i ka puaʻa," wahi a Kealiʻinui. "E kālua ʻia ana ka puaʻa a me nā ʻulu a hiki i ke ahiahi."

I ke ahiahi, ua wehe nā kāne i ka imu. Ua puka mai ka māhu a me ka uahi. Ua wela loa ka puaʻa, no laila ua waiho lākou iā ia no kekahi manawa a maʻalili. "Ke maʻalili ka ʻiʻo, hiki ke ʻoki," wahi a Kealiʻinui. A laila, ua ʻai nā pilikana a pau i ka puaʻa kālua a me ka ʻulu.

I ka lā aʻe, ua hauhau ka ʻiʻo i koe. ʻAʻole ʻono loa ka ʻiʻo hauhau a me ka ʻulu hauhau. No laila, ua hoʻopumehana ʻo Kaʻimikaua i ka ʻiʻo a me ka ʻulu ma luna o ke ahi. Ua ʻai hou nā pilikana. "ʻOno nō ka puaʻa kālua," wahi a Kaʻimikaua, "ʻoiai he puaʻa hauhau ia, ke hoʻopumehana ʻia."

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia kālā i uku ai ʻo Kealiʻinui no ka puaʻa?
Ua uku ʻo ia i 300 kālā no ka puaʻa.
Na wai i hōʻā i ka wahie ma loko o ka imu?
Na Kealiʻinui i hōʻā i ka wahie.
He aha ka mea e kālua ai i ka puaʻa?
ʻO ka māhu ka mea e kālua ai i ka puaʻa.
No ke aha i waiho ai lākou i ka puaʻa ma hope o ka wehe ʻana i ka imu?
No ka mea, ua wela loa ka puaʻa, a pono e maʻalili.
He aha ka hana a Kaʻimikaua i ka ʻiʻo hauhau?
Ua hoʻopumehana ʻo ia i ka ʻiʻo hauhau ma luna o ke ahi.

lessons.title: Ka moʻowaiwai o Kamaile
lessons.summary: Twelve-year-old Kamaile wants a telescope to see an asteroid pass the earth; she opens a bank account, asks the clerk question after question, makes a weekly habit of saving, avoids the shave-ice shop she passes, and buys the telescope in time.
lessons.text:
He 12 makahiki o Kamaile. Ma ke kīwī, ua lohe ʻo ia e kāʻalo ana kekahi hōkūnaʻi nui ma kahi kokoke i ka honua i ka makahiki aʻe. Akā he 300 kālā ke kumukūʻai o kekahi ʻohe nānā maikaʻi. No laila, ua hele ʻo ia me kona makuahine i ka panakō e wehe i kekahi moʻowaiwai.

Ua piʻi lāua i nā ʻanuʻu pōhaku o ka panakō kahiko ma ke kaona. Ua lelele ka puʻuwai o Kamaile i kona piʻi ʻana i nā ʻanuʻu. Ma loko, ua ninaninau ʻo ia i ka wahine o ka panakō: "Pehea e mālama ʻia ai kaʻu kālā?" "Ke ninaninau nei ʻoe iaʻu e like me kekahi loio!" wahi a ka wahine me ka ʻakaʻaka. Ua lawe ʻo Kamaile i kekahi penikala e kākau i kona inoa, akā ua ʻōlelo ka wahine, "ʻAʻole hiki ke kākau me ka penikala ma kēia pepa."

Ua lawe mai ʻo Kamaile i kāna ipu kālā. Ua kaumaha loa ia: he 46 kālā. Ua waiho ʻia ke kālā i loko o ka moʻowaiwai hou, a ua hoʻomāmā ʻia ka ipu. "Ua hoʻomāmā ʻoe i kāu ipu kālā, a ua hoʻokaumaha ʻoe i kāu moʻowaiwai," wahi a ka wahine me ka minoʻaka.

Mai ia lā mai, ua lilo kekahi hana i mea kūmau na Kamaile: i kēlā me kēia Pōʻalima, hele ʻo ia i ka panakō me 10 kālā. Ma kona ala kūmau i ka panakō, kāʻalo ʻo ia i kekahi hale kūʻai hau kahi. Ke kāʻalo ʻo ia i laila, ʻike ʻo ia i nā keiki me ka hau kahi e heheʻe ana ma ko lākou mau lima. No laila, hōʻalo ʻo ia i ka hale kūʻai.

Ma hope o ʻeono mahina, ua lawa ke kālā o ka moʻowaiwai, a ua kūʻai ʻo Kamaile i ka ʻohe nānā. I ka pō i kāʻalo ai ka hōkūnaʻi, ua ʻike ʻo ia iā ia: he kiko liʻiliʻi e neʻe ana ma waena o nā hōkū. Ua lelele kona puʻuwai. I ka lā aʻe, ua kūʻai ʻo ia i kekahi hau kahi, a ua heheʻe ia ma kona lima. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i hōʻalo hou i ka hale kūʻai.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka mea a Kamaile i makemake ai e ʻike?
Makemake ʻo ia e ʻike i ka hōkūnaʻi.
No ke aha ʻaʻole hiki iā Kamaile ke kākau me ka penikala?
No ka mea, ʻaʻole hiki ke kākau me ka penikala ma ka pepa o ka panakō.
He aha ka hana kūmau a Kamaile i kēlā me kēia Pōʻalima?
Hele ʻo ia i ka panakō me 10 kālā.
No ke aha i hōʻalo ai ʻo Kamaile i ka hale kūʻai hau kahi?
No ka mea, makemake ʻo ia e mālama i kāna kālā no ka ʻohe nānā.

lessons.title: Ka wai noni ma ka mākeke
lessons.summary: Keʻalaonaona sells her own noni juice at the Saturday market in Kailua; an arrogant newcomer, Kaʻehukai, boasts that his juice cures everything, pesters the shoppers and bullies her, until a visitor with an allergy reacts to his juice, his lie comes out and he has to apologise.
lessons.text:
Kūʻai aku ʻo Keʻalaonaona i ka wai noni ma ka mākeke o ka Pōʻaono ma Kailua. Ulu nā kumu noni ma kona ʻāina ma uka. Hana ʻo ia i ka wai noni me kona mau lima ponoʻī. He 10 kālā ka ipu.

I kekahi Pōʻaono, ua hele mai kekahi kanaka hou ma kahi kokoke iā ia; ʻo Kaʻehukai kona inoa. Ua kūʻai aku ʻo ia i ka wai noni no 30 kālā ka ipu. He kanaka ʻaʻano ʻo Kaʻehukai. Ua kaena ʻo ia i nā kānaka a pau: "Hoʻōla kaʻu wai noni i nā maʻi a pau!"

Ua hoʻouluhua ʻo Kaʻehukai i nā kānaka. Ua kāhea leo nui ʻo ia i nā mea a pau e hele ana, a ua paʻa ʻo ia i ko lākou mau lima. ʻAʻano ʻo ia, a ua hoʻomaʻau pū ʻo ia iā Keʻalaonaona. "He wai ʻino kāu wai noni," wahi āna. "Mai kūʻai iā ia!" ʻAʻole ʻo Keʻalaonaona i pane aku.

I kekahi lā, ua inu kekahi wahine malihini i ka wai noni a Kaʻehukai. Ma hope iho, ua ʻulaʻula kona ʻili, a ua pehu kona mau lima. "He pāheu koʻu i kekahi mau mea ʻai," wahi a ka wahine. "Ua ʻōlelo mai ʻoe he noni wale nō kēia!" Ua heluhelu ʻo Keʻalaonaona i ka ipu: aia nā mea ʻē aʻe he nui i loko o ka wai noni a Kaʻehukai. Ua wahaheʻe ʻo ia. Ua hoʻomālie ʻo Keʻalaonaona i ka wahine, a ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i ka wai maʻemaʻe nāna e inu.

Ua hele mai ka luna o ka mākeke, a ua hoʻomālie ʻo ia i nā kānaka. "Ua wahaheʻe ʻoe i kēia wahine," wahi āna iā Kaʻehukai, "a ua hoʻouluhua ʻoe i nā kānaka a pau. Inā ʻaʻole ʻoe e mihi, ʻaʻole hiki iā ʻoe ke hoʻi mai." Ua mihi ʻo Kaʻehukai. "E kala mai iaʻu. Ua mihi au no kaʻu wahaheʻe." Ua ʻaka nā kānaka e kū ana ma laila i kāna mau ʻōlelo kaena mua.

Mai ia lā mai, ua kūʻai nā kānaka he nui i ka wai noni a Keʻalaonaona. Ke kaena kekahi kanaka ʻē aʻe no kāna noni, ʻaka ʻo Keʻalaonaona.

Nā nīnau:
Pehea ʻo Kaʻehukai i kaena ai?
Ua kaena ʻo ia, hoʻōla kāna wai noni i nā maʻi a pau.
He aha ka mea i loaʻa i ka wahine malihini ma hope o kona inu ʻana?
Ua ʻulaʻula kona ʻili, a ua pehu kona mau lima, no ka mea he pāheu kona.
Na wai i hoʻomaʻau iā Keʻalaonaona?
Na Kaʻehukai i hoʻomaʻau iā ia.
He aha ka mea a ka luna o ka mākeke i ʻōlelo ai?
Inā ʻaʻole ʻo Kaʻehukai e mihi, ʻaʻole hiki iā ia ke hoʻi mai.

lessons.title: Nā mea kanu o Kalawai
lessons.summary: Kekahu buys plants for the empty garden of his new house in Makawao from Kalawai's nursery: a ginkgo from China, a fully grown Hawaiian cotton with a caterpillar on its leaves and two young manono; at home he ties the young trees to stakes, and when the cloudy sky clears the stream runs fast.
lessons.text:
Ua kūʻai ʻo Kekahu i kekahi hale hou ma Makawao. ʻAʻohe lāʻau ma kona māla. I kekahi kakahiaka ʻōmalumalu, ua hele ʻo ia i ka hale kūʻai mea kanu o Kalawai e kūʻai i nā lāʻau no kona māla. ʻŌmalumalu ka lani, a ua hāʻule iki ka ua.

Ua hōʻike ʻo Kalawai iā ia i kekahi lāʻau ʻano ʻē, me nā lau like me ka peʻahi. "He nanahana kēia," wahi āna. "No Kina mai ka nanahana. He lāʻau kahiko loa ia ma ka honua." Ua makemake ʻo Kekahu i ka nanahana. He 60 kālā kona kumukūʻai.

"Makemake pū au i nā mea kanu ʻōiwi o Hawaiʻi," wahi a Kekahu. Ua hōʻike ʻo Kalawai iā ia i ka maʻo me kona mau pua melemele, a me ka manono, he lāʻau liʻiliʻi o ka ululāʻau. "Ua mōhāhā kēia maʻo," wahi a Kalawai. "Ua nui kona mau lālā, a ua mōhāhā kona mau pua. He ʻōpio naʻe kēia mau manono; ʻaʻole lākou i mōhāhā." Ua kūʻai ʻo Kekahu i ka maʻo mōhāhā a me ʻelua manono ʻōpio, no 45 kālā.

Ma kekahi lau o ka maʻo, ua ʻike ʻo Kekahu i kekahi hē ʻōmaʻomaʻo. "Ke ʻai nei ka hē i nā lau!" wahi āna. "Mai hopohopo, he hē liʻiliʻi wale nō," wahi a Kalawai. "E ʻai ana ka hē i kekahi mau lau, akā e ola ana ka maʻo." Ua lawe ʻo ia i ka hē, a ua waiho iā ia ma kekahi lāʻau ʻē aʻe.

Ma ka hale, ua kanu ʻo Kekahu i nā lāʻau. He ʻōpio ka nanahana, a hiki paha iā ia ke hina i ka makani. No laila, ua hoʻokū ʻo ia i kekahi koʻo lāʻau ma ka ʻaoʻao o ka nanahana, a ua nākiʻi ʻo ia i ka nanahana i ke koʻo me kekahi kaula palupalu. Ua nākiʻi pū ʻo ia i kēlā me kēia manono i kekahi koʻo liʻiliʻi.

I ke awakea, ua mao ka ua, a ua mao pū nā ao. ʻAʻole ʻōmalumalu hou ka lani. Ma hope o ka māla, ua kikī ka wai o ke kahawai liʻiliʻi, no ka mea ua nui ka ua o ke kakahiaka.

Nā nīnau:
No hea mai ka nanahana?
No Kina mai ka nanahana.
He aha ka mea e ʻai ana i nā lau o ka maʻo?
He hē liʻiliʻi ʻōmaʻomaʻo.
No ke aha i nākiʻi ai ʻo Kekahu i ka nanahana i ke koʻo?
No ka mea he ʻōpio ka nanahana, a hiki paha iā ia ke hina i ka makani.
No ke aha i kikī ai ka wai o ke kahawai?
No ka mea ua nui ka ua o ke kakahiaka.

lessons.title: Ka malo no ka hula
lessons.summary: Kapiliʻula's son Kahoʻokano will dance in a hula contest in Kahului; a ready-made loincloth costs eighty dollars, so she buys cloth and thread for fifteen and sews it by hand, pricking her finger and breaking a nail, and the malo is ready for the contest.
lessons.text:
E hula ana ʻo Kahoʻokano, ke keiki a Kapiliʻula, i ka hula kahiko ma kekahi hoʻokūkū ma Kahului. Pono iā ia kekahi malo. Ma ka hale kūʻai, ua ʻike lāua i nā malo i humuhumu ʻia, akā he 80 kālā ke kumukūʻai o ka malo. "Pipiʻi loa kēlā," wahi a Kapiliʻula. "Naʻu nō e humuhumu i kou malo."

Ua kūʻai ʻo ia i kekahi ʻāpana lole ʻulaʻula lōʻihi a me ka lopi ʻulaʻula, no 15 kālā wale nō. I ka pō, ua noho ʻo ia ma ka pākaukau me ka lole, ka lopi a me kekahi kui humuhumu. Ua ʻoki ʻo ia i kekahi maʻawe lopi lōʻihi, a ua hoʻokomo ʻo ia i ka maʻawe i loko o ka maka o ke kui. ʻAʻole maʻalahi ka hana: ua liʻiliʻi loa ka maka o ke kui, a ua palupalu ka maʻawe.

Ua humuhumu ʻo Kapiliʻula ma ka lima, a ua humuhumu ʻo ia no nā hola he nui. Ma kekahi manawa, ua ʻō ke kui i kona manamana lima. Ua ʻehaʻeha kona manamana, a ua kahe iki ke koko. Ma hope iho, ua haki kekahi mikiʻao ona i kona huki ʻana i ka lopi. Ua ʻehaʻeha hou kona manamana. Ua pala ʻo ia i kekahi ʻaila lapaʻau ma ka manamana, a ua ʻoki ʻo ia i ka mikiʻao i haki.

I ke kakahiaka, ua ala mai ʻo Kahoʻokano, a ua ʻike ʻo ia i kona makuahine e humuhumu ana. "Ua hiamoe ʻoe, e Māmā?" i nīnau ai ʻo ia. "ʻAʻole nui," wahi āna. Ua kōkua ʻo Kahoʻokano: ua paʻa ʻo ia i ka lole, a ua humuhumu ʻo Kapiliʻula i ka maʻawe hope loa. Ua pala hou ʻo ia i ka ʻaila ma kona manamana, a ua ʻakaʻaka lāua.

Ua komo ʻo Kahoʻokano i ka malo. Ua kūpono ia iā ia. Ma ka hoʻokūkū, ua hula ʻo ia me nā kāne ʻē aʻe o kona hālau, a ua ʻulaʻula nā malo a pau. ʻAʻole i ʻike ka poʻe e nānā ana, ua humuhumu ʻia kona malo ma ka hale.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ke kumukūʻai o ka malo ma ka hale kūʻai?
He 80 kālā ke kumukūʻai o ka malo.
He aha nā mea a Kapiliʻula i kūʻai ai?
Ua kūʻai ʻo ia i kekahi ʻāpana lole ʻulaʻula a me ka lopi ʻulaʻula.
No ke aha i ʻehaʻeha ai kona manamana?
No ka mea, ua ʻō ke kui i kona manamana lima.
He aha ka mea i haki i kona huki ʻana i ka lopi?
Ua haki kekahi mikiʻao ona.
Pehea ʻo Kahoʻokano i kōkua ai i kona makuahine?
Ua paʻa ʻo ia i ka lole ʻoiai ʻo Kapiliʻula e humuhumu ana i ka maʻawe hope loa.

lessons.title: Ka hōʻikeʻike ma ka pākaua kahiko
lessons.summary: Kaʻaihue and his wife Waileia take a small train along an old sugar railroad to a craft fair in an old fort on a peninsula; an old man sells stone kōnane boards with pebbles he blackened, a woman shapes pots with a shining glaze, and an old tortoise-shell comb is shown but not for sale.
lessons.text:
I kekahi Lāpule, ua hele ʻo Kaʻaihue a me kāna wahine ʻo Waileia i kekahi hōʻikeʻike hana noʻeau. Mālama ʻia ka hōʻikeʻike ma loko o kekahi pākaua kahiko ma kekahi ʻanemoku liʻiliʻi. I ka wā kahiko, ua kūkulu nā koa i ka pākaua ma ka ʻanemoku, no ka mea hiki ke ʻike ʻia nā moku o ka ʻenemi mai laila aku.

ʻAʻohe alanui i ka ʻanemoku. Aia wale nō kekahi alahao kahiko, a holo kekahi kaʻaahi liʻiliʻi ma luna o ke alahao. Ua kūkulu ʻia kēia alahao no ke kō ma mua o ka makahiki 1900. Ua uku lāua i 5 kālā, a ua holo lāua ma ke kaʻaahi ma ke alahao.

Ma loko o ka pākaua, aia nā pākaukau kūʻai he nui. Ma kekahi pākaukau, noho kekahi ʻelemakule. Kūʻai aku ka ʻelemakule i nā papamū pōhaku no ka pāʻani kōnane. Ua kālai ʻo ia i nā lua liʻiliʻi he nui ma luna o kēlā me kēia papamū. "Pāʻani ʻia ke kōnane me nā ʻiliʻili ʻeleʻele a me nā ʻiliʻili keʻokeʻo," wahi a ka ʻelemakule. "Keʻokeʻo kēia mau ʻiliʻili mai kahakai mai, no laila ua pāʻele au i kekahi o lākou me ka pena ʻeleʻele." Ua kūʻai ʻo Kaʻaihue i kekahi papamū liʻiliʻi a me nā ʻiliʻili i pāʻele ʻia, no 40 kālā. Ua pāʻani ʻo ia i ke kōnane me ka ʻelemakule, a ua lanakila ka ʻelemakule.

Ma kekahi pākaukau ʻē aʻe, ua hana kekahi wahine i nā ipu pokela. Ua hōʻano ʻo ia i ka pālolo i ipu me kona mau lima. Ua ʻalohi nā ipu pokela i ka lā, me he wai lā. Ua kūʻai ʻo Waileia i kekahi ipu pokela uliuli e ʻalohi ana e like me ke kai, no 30 kālā.

Ma ka hope o ka hōʻikeʻike, aia kekahi kahi lauoho kahiko i hana ʻia me ka una o ka honu. "ʻAʻole kūʻai ʻia kēia," wahi a ka wahine nona ia. "Na koʻu kupuna wahine kēia kahi una. I kēia wā, ua pāpā ʻia ke kūʻai ʻana i ka una o ka honu."

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i kūkulu ai nā koa i ka pākaua ma ka ʻanemoku?
No ka mea, hiki ke ʻike ʻia nā moku o ka ʻenemi mai laila aku.
He aha ka hana a ka ʻelemakule i nā ʻiliʻili keʻokeʻo?
Ua pāʻele ʻo ia i kekahi o lākou me ka pena ʻeleʻele.
He aha ka mea a ka wahine i hōʻano ai me kona mau lima?
Ua hōʻano ʻo ia i ka pālolo i ipu.
No ke aha ʻaʻole i kūʻai ʻia ke kahi una?
No ka mea, ua pāpā ʻia ke kūʻai ʻana i ka una o ka honu.

lessons.title: Ka papakema o Kaleikaumaka
lessons.summary: Malulani tells how she bought a white outfit and cookies for the baptism of her baby nephew Kaleikaumaka in Kāneʻohe: she holds him, he wets her dress, the minister baptizes him in the name of the triune God, and at the party the baby drinks milk while the children scatter cookie crumbs.
lessons.text:
ʻO Malulani koʻu inoa. I ka mahina i hala, ua hānau ʻia kekahi keiki kāne na koʻu kaikunāne ʻo Kamakaʻike a me kāna wahine ʻo Kalikoʻula, koʻu kaikoʻeke. ʻO Kaleikaumaka ka inoa o ka pēpē. Ua kono mai koʻu kaikoʻeke iaʻu i ka papakema o ka pēpē ma ka hale pule ma Kāneʻohe.

Ma mua o ka papakema, ua hele au i ka hale kūʻai e kūʻai i kekahi makana. Ua kūʻai au i kekahi lole keʻokeʻo liʻiliʻi no ka pēpē, no 35 kālā. Ua kūʻai pū au i kanaono kuki no ka pāʻina ma hope o ka papakema. He 12 kālā nā kuki.

Ma ka hale pule, ua hiʻi au i ka pēpē ma koʻu mau lima ʻoiai koʻu kaikoʻeke e hoʻoponopono ana i kona lole. Ua ʻulaʻula nā pāpālina o ka pēpē, a ua momona nō hoʻi kona mau pāpālina. Ua pā mālie au i kona mau pāpālina me koʻu manamana. A laila, ua mimi ka pēpē! Ua pulu koʻu lole. Ua ʻakaʻaka koʻu kaikoʻeke. "Ua mimi ʻo ia iā ʻoe! ʻO ia kona aloha iā ʻoe," wahi āna.

Ua papekema ke kahu i ka pēpē. Ua kau ʻo ia i ka wai ma luna o kona poʻo, a ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia, "Ke papekema nei au iā ʻoe ma ka inoa o ka Makua, a me ke Keiki, a me ka ʻUhane Hemolele." Ua wehewehe ke kahu i ka poʻe: "Hoʻokahi wale nō Akua, akā ʻekolu ʻano: ʻo ia ke Akua Kahikolu." Ua kani ka leo o ka pēpē i ka wā i papekema ʻia ai ʻo ia, a ua hiʻi koʻu kaikunāne iā ia.

Ma hope o ka papakema, aia ka pāʻina ma ka hale o koʻu kaikunāne. Ua inu ka pēpē i ka waiū, a ua hiamoe ʻo ia ma nā lima o kona makuahine. Ua ʻai nā keiki i nā kuki a ua inu lākou i ka waiū anuanu. Ua hāʻule nā hunahuna kuki ma ka papahele a pau. Ma hope o ka pāʻina, ua kāhili au i nā hunahuna, a ua hiʻi hou au i ka pēpē.

Nā nīnau:
ʻO wai ke kaikoʻeke o Malulani?
ʻO Kalikoʻula, ka wahine a kona kaikunāne, ke kaikoʻeke o Malulani.
He aha nā mea a Malulani i kūʻai ai no ka papakema?
Ua kūʻai ʻo ia i kekahi lole keʻokeʻo liʻiliʻi a me kanaono kuki.
He aha ka mea i hana ʻia e ka pēpē ma ka hale pule?
Ua mimi ka pēpē, a ua pulu ka lole o Malulani.
He aha ke Akua Kahikolu, wahi a ke kahu?
Hoʻokahi wale nō Akua, akā ʻekolu ʻano.
He aha ka mea i hāʻule ma ka papahele?
Ua hāʻule nā hunahuna kuki ma ka papahele.

lessons.title: Ka ake a ka luahine
lessons.summary: After the funeral of his grandmother Kahaleʻula, an old woman of ninety-four mourned with a chanted lament, Kamealoha buys beef liver and turmeric at the market, sifts flour and fries her favourite dish on the stove, feels her spirit near, and sets out a plate as an offering.
lessons.text:
Ua make ke kupuna wahine o Kamealoha, ʻo Kahaleʻula, i ka mahina ʻo ʻAukake. He luahine ʻo ia: he 94 ona makahiki. I ka lā i kanu ʻia ai ʻo ia, ua oli kekahi ʻanakala i kekahi kanikau nona. Ua lohe ʻo Kamealoha i ka leo o ke kanikau, a ua kahe kona waimaka.

Ma hope o ka lā kanu, ua hoʻomanaʻo ʻo Kamealoha i ka mea ʻai punahele a ka luahine: ka ake pipi i palai ʻia me ka lena a me nā ʻakaʻakai. Ua kuke pinepine ka luahine i ia mea ʻai i ka Lāpule. No laila, ua hele ʻo Kamealoha i ka mākeke. Ua kūʻai ʻo ia i ʻelua paona ake pipi no 8 kālā, a me kekahi ʻeke lena melemele no 4 kālā.

Ma ka hale, ua kālana ʻo ia i ka palaoa i loko o kekahi ipu, e like me kāna i ʻike ai i ka luahine e hana ana. Ua hoʻohui ʻo ia i ka lena i ka palaoa i kālana ʻia, a ua lilo ka palaoa i ka melemele. Ua kau ʻo ia i ka ake i loko o ka palaoa melemele. A laila, ua hōʻā ʻo ia i ke kapuahi, a ua palai ʻo ia i ka ake me nā ʻakaʻakai ma luna o ke kapuahi.

Ua piha ka hale i ka ʻala o ka ake a me ka lena. Ua kū ʻo Kamealoha ma ka ʻaoʻao o ke kapuahi, a ua manaʻo ʻo ia aia ka wailua o kona kupuna wahine ma ka lumi kuke me ia. "Aloha, e Tūtū," wahi āna, me ka waimaka ma kona maka.

Ua kau ʻo ia i kekahi pā ake ma ka pākaukau, ma ka ʻaoʻao o ke kiʻi o ka luahine. "He hai kēia nou, e Tūtū," wahi āna. Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i kēia hai i ka wailua o kona kupuna. A laila, ua ʻai ʻo ia i ka ake. ʻOno loa ia, akā ʻaʻole like loa me ka ake a ka luahine.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia makahiki o ka luahine?
He 94 ona makahiki.
Na wai i oli i ke kanikau?
Na kekahi ʻanakala i oli i ke kanikau.
He aha ka mea ʻai punahele a ka luahine?
ʻO ka ake pipi i palai ʻia me ka lena a me nā ʻakaʻakai.
He aha ka hana a Kamealoha i ka palaoa?
Ua kālana ʻo ia i ka palaoa, a ua hoʻohui ʻo ia i ka lena.
He aha ka mea a Kamealoha i kau ai ma ka ʻaoʻao o ke kiʻi o ka luahine?
Ua kau ʻo ia i kekahi pā ake ma laila, he hai no ka wailua o kona kupuna.
